findings.title: Covert Listening Becomes a Counterfeit Frame
findings.claim: Hearing is captured by a covert social frame: the charge labels the messenger, and 17:48 identifies comparison-making as a route to straying and inability to find a way.
findings.mechanism: The focus's repeated hearing and secret counsel meet the spoken charge; 17:48 returns through examples, straying, and an unreachable path. The description can therefore act as a counterfeit explanation rather than engagement with the message. The represented HFT before-reading is: ‘The phrase 'enchanted man' is a free-standing insult.’ Its changed reading is: ‘It is a failed explanatory analogy: their listening produces a frame that seems to classify the messenger but disables further orientation.’ The represented roles retain verbal attribution, deception, inspection, comparison, straying, and path-loss.
findings.reader_payoff: Covert hearing, group interpretation, and public accusation become one locally connected process whose own comparison-making loses its route.
findings.containment: The ordinary floor remains intact: “Seni nasıl dinlediklerini en iyi biz biliriz; seni dinledikleri ve kendi aralarında gizlice konuştukları sırada zalimler, 'Siz ancak büyülenmiş bir adama uyuyorsunuz' derler.” The charge is not endorsed; the human referent remains ordinary; path-loss is adjacent, not etymology. The due-share branch is excluded. Source qualification: The packet supplies the focus accusation and the adjacent command to inspect their comparisons; I infer that 'enchanted man' is one of those comparisons and that framing causes the path-loss. The plural may also gather accusations not stated in the focus ayah.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence is anchored in 17:47-48; represented legacy-unbound HFT roles remain attributed.

findings.title: Reception Through a Layered Filter
findings.claim: Against the preceding barriers, repeated listening can remain audible reception while failing to mature into understanding or uptake.
findings.mechanism: 17:44 contrasts the world's praise with failure to understand; 17:45 places a veil between recitation and listeners; 17:46 names covered hearts, burdened ears, and withdrawal. These distinguish sound reaching the listeners from their receiving its import. Before-reading: “They hear the recitation but refuse its content.” Changed reading: “They listen through a layered filter: sound reaches the ear, but covered understanding turns reception into aversion and preserves noncompliance.”
findings.reader_payoff: Audible contact and responsive uptake become perceptibly different events.
findings.containment: The ordinary listening-and-refusal reading remains. Filtering is contextual, not a claim that sound is absent; direct imposed incapacity remains possible. Source qualification: The packet supplies successive external, inward, auditory, and bodily obstructions; I infer that they specify the operative means or manner in the focus construction 'بما يستمعون به'. A live alternative is direct imposed incapacity rather than a self-reinforcing interpretive filter.

epistemic.reason: Exact pericope coordinates and roots align, but the causal synthesis is legacy-unbound HFT attribution.

findings.title: A Material Objection Reframes the Accusation
findings.claim: The “bewitched man” charge can defend a familiar material expectation by locating abnormality in the messenger before the pericope develops an objection from remains and harder matter.
findings.mechanism: 17:49 raises fragments and bones, 17:50 escalates to stone or iron, and 17:51 answers with first origination. This sequence meets the focus's personal diagnosis, but does not state an explicit causal link. Before-reading: “The enchanted-man charge is a generic attack on credibility.” Changed reading: “It can function as an ontology-defense: a claim that exceeds familiar material measurement is neutralized by locating the abnormality in its human bearer.”
findings.reader_payoff: A diagnosis of the speaker can be perceived as shielding an expectation about what kinds of bodies can return.
findings.containment: The accusation remains an accusation. The resurrection exchange may be separate, with no causal tie to the focus; no doctrine is selected. Source qualification: The packet supplies the accusation followed by a tightly developed material objection; I infer that the label protects the objectors' ontology by pathologizing its challenger. The alternative is that the resurrection exchange begins a separate objection with no specific causal tie to the accusation.

epistemic.reason: Coordinates align, but linking the accusation to the later material objection is explicitly inferential.

findings.title: Listening Measured by Its Response
findings.claim: The focus listening can be read as incomplete reception when it issues in private counsel and accusation, beside 17:52's call followed immediately by an answer.
findings.mechanism: 17:52 supplies a response-shaped comparison for the focus sequence from listening through counsel to speech. findings.title: A Seeker-Side Path Overlay
findings.claim: Fātiḥa 1:6-1:7 adds a communal seeking voice beside the focus's “following” and native 17:48's lost path: a request for guidance on a straight path and a path marked by favor rather than anger or straying.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier تتبعون meets the external guidance/path request; 17:48 makes the contact local through its route-loss. The scene gains a seeker-side question of orientation without assigning the Messenger the role of the favored path.

findings.containment: This phase-two overlay uses only 1:6-1:7. It does not equate the Messenger with the favored path, identify a group as its referent, or import a whole-surah reading.

epistemic.reason: Exact external path and guidance occurrences contact the focus follow-branch and 17:48, but the juxtaposition remains exploratory.
